2) Retention windows and whether they can be shortened or disabled for the PoC.
3) Who has access to stored records and how logs/audit trails are provided for your security review.
4) Residency and KMS options for data-at-rest.

Hi Anna / James — answers below so you can paste into the internal security/legal notes. I kept this intentionally concise and actionable.

Q1 — What we persist (hosted API default):
- Prompts and model outputs: by default Redwood stores full request and response text for up to 30 days to support debugging, safety reviews, and quality monitoring. Stored fields include: request body (prompt text), response body (generated tokens), timestamp, model id/version, route metadata. Network headers are not routinely stored (we store only routing metadata unless customer opts to log additional request headers).
- We can enable an explicit "ephemeral" mode for prompts/outputs where no durable copy is written (TTL=0). This is selectable at account or route level and is what we propose for your PoC if you want zero retention.

Q2 — Embeddings:
- Embeddings are NOT stored by default unless you enable indexing/semantic search features. If enabled, embeddings are persisted to a customer-scoped index which you can configure to use your KMS and to be hosted in-region. For the PoC, we will keep embeddings disabled unless you explicitly request them.

Q3 — Access controls & KMS:
- Hosted API: Redwood engineers have no default access to customer data; access is gated through RBAC and audited. Emergency access requires a documented approval workflow and is logged.
- Options: customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/HSM) for encryption-at-rest and per-tenant key separation.

Q4 — Retention windows & audit logs:
- Default: 30 days for hosted telemetry (prompts/outputs).
- Configurable: retention can be shortened to custom TTLs, including 0 days (ephemeral). Dedicated and Private deployments: retention is controlled by the customer — Redwood does not retain prompts/outputs in our hosted stores unless explicitly configured.
- Audit logs: We provide exportable audit logs (JSON/CSV) showing read/write events, user/service principal, timestamp, and action. Standard retention for audit trail exports: 13 months; can be exported on-demand to your S3.

Q5 — Residency:
- We support region pinning for storage and compute. For hosted PoC we will pin to us-east-1. Private deployments can be fully on-prem or in your VPC.

Caching and KV stores: short-lived KV/prefix caches used for latency optimization are in-memory by default and are not persisted to durable storage unless configured for long-running session state.

Next steps we propose (concrete):
- Redwood sends: DPA addendum draft + SOC2 snapshot (attached). Marissa will follow up with SOC2 excerpt.
- Agreement on PoC config: TTL=0 (ephemeral) for prompts/outputs, embeddings disabled, region us-east-1, 30-day evaluation.
- Kickoff: Apr 2 — technical handoff with your engineering (30–60 minutes).

If you want, I can produce a one-page technical appendix that Legal can insert into the SOW (I can have that to you by Monday).

—
